author: maintainer-agent

patch.value:
## Problem
The active graph reports zero isolates and zero degree-one nodes, which reads as healthy. It is not the property that matters. What matters for an agent is whether a traversal from an item reaches an outcome that explains it, and how many typed hops that takes. A workspace can be fully connected and still be a flat list wearing a graph costume.

## What good looks like
From any active item, following typed edges reaches an outcome milestone; the path passes through the epic that owns the capability, the feature that delivers it, and the decision that authorised it; and each hop is explainable from the edge kind alone. That is depth, and depth is what makes graph algorithms useful for context assembly rather than decorative.

## Measures to add
Depth distribution and eccentricity per active node; shortest typed path to any outcome milestone; edge-kind diversity along that path; count of nodes reachable only through a single parent edge; component structure of the active subgraph excluding parent edges, which is the honest test of semantic linkage.

## Boundary
No density targets and no fabricated edges. An unreachable item is a signal that either an anchor is missing or the item should not be active — both are answers, and both are better than an invented edge.
Strategic reachability invariant: every active item resolves to an outcome milestone through a typed, explainable path within a bounded hop count

The audit profile reports depth distribution, eccentricity, and shortest-path-to-milestone for every active item, not just isolate and degree counts; A declared policy states the maximum acceptable hop distance to an outcome milestone and the minimum distinct edge-kind count on the path; Violations surface as audit findings with a remediation hint naming candidate anchors, never as an instruction to fabricate an edge; Deliberately shallow items are representable as reviewed waivers with recorded rationale rather than silently failing; The profile is computed within the graph analytics token and latency budgets and stays bounded at million-item scale
Graph algorithms alone can answer why any item exists and which outcome it serves

The graph currently guarantees that no active item is isolated. That is a floor, not a structure: an item can satisfy it with one parent edge and still be unreachable from any strategic outcome, which means no traversal can explain why it is being worked on.

Turns the relationship graph from a connectivity artifact into a navigable explanation of the project, which is the precondition for graph-driven context assembly and for the reachability-based relevance signals the context engine wants.
A governance profile reports, for every active item, the shortest typed path to an outcome milestone and the edge-kind diversity along it; violations are findings with named owners.

Outcome milestones now exist as graph roots, so reachability finally has a defined target. Measuring depth before the terminal-history backfill waves run means the waves can be aimed at the actual gaps.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Reachability and depth baseline measured 2026-07-25 over all 2,027 items, for the bounded-hop invariant this item declares.

Active set (255 items), semantic edges only, breadth-first from the six outcome milestones:
- unreachable: 0
- depth histogram: 6 at depth 0 (the milestones), 85 at 1, 98 at 2, 25 at 3, 8 at 4, 10 at 5, 23 at 6
- maximum semantic depth: 6

Including hierarchy edges the maximum falls to 4, which is the expected result and worth stating explicitly: the parent tree is a shortcut, so any invariant measured over all edges will look healthier than the project actually is. The semantic-only measurement is the honest one and should be what this item gates on.

Two observations for the invariant's design:

1. A third of the active set (85 of 255) sits at semantic depth 1 — attached directly to an outcome milestone. That is a legacy of earlier enrichment passes that optimised for eliminating unreachable items, and direct attachment was the cheapest way to do it. It satisfies a reachability invariant while conveying little: an edge from a Semgrep finding straight to "provable history" explains nothing about the path between them. Recommend this item's acceptance criteria include a *minimum* explanatory path quality, not only a maximum hop count — for instance that the path from an execution item to its outcome traverses its capability epic rather than bypassing it.

2. Edge-kind distribution across the whole graph is heavily skewed toward the generic: related 2,007, parent 1,852, blocked_by 364, blocks 69, discovered_from 55, verifies 25, implements 15, child 15, incident_from 1. The typed kinds that carry real planning semantics — implements and verifies — account for 40 of 4,403 edges, under one percent. A bounded-hop invariant computed over `related` edges is close to a connectivity check; computed over typed edges it is a genuine claim about how work reaches an outcome. Recommend the invariant declare which kinds count as explanatory and measure only those.

Active-graph degree is saturated: exactly 28 active items carry a semantic degree of one or less, and all 28 are Semgrep findings whose deliberate hub topology routes through per-file and per-rule representatives. No honest edge remains to be added there, and none should be fabricated.

value.text: Baseline and first movement measured 2026-07-26, so this invariant now has a number to enforce rather than an aspiration. Before: the six outcome milestones carried almost no inbound typed edges — pm graph impact <milestone> --kind implements,verifies --direction incoming returned 1, 0, 0, 1, 5 and 2 nodes for j82fd3, 9rgaal, w7ccmv, o87av6, xp1xsw and t4d7nz respectively. The strategic layer was wired with the untyped related kind (2,089 edges) which no traversal treats as semantic, so 'every active item resolves to an outcome milestone' was unmeasurable, not merely unmet. After a three-wave typed-edge pass over open items only (implements 49 to 286, verifies 41 to 91, total edges 4,558 to 4,877, zero new cycles, zero new audit findings): reach per milestone is 61, 36, 22, 49, 123 and 16 at shortest-path distances up to 5, and 268 of 271 active items reach at least one outcome. The three that do not are the outcome milestones themselves, which are roots. Two structural notes for this item's gate design. First, the parent hierarchy alone cannot satisfy this invariant: parent chains terminate at pm-doxj, the roadmap root, which is not an outcome, so the typed layer is load-bearing rather than redundant with hierarchy. Second, the four items that needed hand-wiring were exactly those whose parent is closed (pm-5ecnar under pm-pim7, pm-5sm91o under pm-j36ypd) or whose parent is the roadmap root (pm-95d7), which identifies the two structural cases a gate must handle rather than treat as one-offs.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Depth baseline for the terminal corpus, measured 2026-07-26 during the relationship backfill, so this item has real numbers to build its metrics on rather than active-only ones.

Before the pass, over 1,795 terminal items: 1,024 had no outbound edge at all, 822 had none in either direction, 1,682 had no edge of any kind that semantic traversal accepts, and 184 had no parent. The active graph reported 0 isolates and 0 degree-at-most-one nodes at the same moment, which is the exact illusion this item exists to correct — active-scoped depth metrics certified a healthy graph while 86 percent of the workspace was unreachable.

Evidence classes and their yield, for whoever builds the coverage profile: typed hierarchy mirror 1,607 edges, explicit identifier references in durable text 2,244 edges, shared linked artifact 45 edges, shared issue reference 2 edges. The steep fall-off after the first two classes is itself a finding — artefact and issue co-reference add almost nothing once hierarchy and explicit references are exhausted, so a future completeness metric should weight those two classes heavily and treat the others as tie-breakers rather than as independent coverage dimensions.

Reachability after the pass, single-node probe: graph impact from closed item pm-00yy in the outgoing direction reaches 1,444 nodes across 9,568 inspected edges, from a node that previously had no traversable outbound edge at all. That is the depth this item wants to measure, and it is now measurable.
